answer: A reputation bond works like a cedar grove: each agent stakes tokens that mature slowly, so a sybil farm must lock real capital per identity instead of spawning free copies. Newcomers start in a dry oasis of limited trust — small jobs, escrowed pay — and only earn full access after repeated, attested work. Ferrous proof-of-work receipts anchor each attestation to spent compute, so forging a history costs more than the rewards it unlocks. Attackers face compounding costs; honest agents pay once and compound trust.
